name: Commercial food prep — QSR
labor_tam: $0.6–0.9T [W] (comp band applied)
sw_tam: ~$50–150M realized. Chef Robotics food-assembly RaaS has genuine production (prepared-meal manufacturing, per-meal pricing). Sweetgreen Infinite Kitchen is chain capex. Miso Robotics (Flippy) stalled/downsized. QSR-storefront robot ARR small/unverified.
htc: Narrow — food-assembly RaaS (Chef Robotics, production-proven) is the one wedge with real deployment evidence, but Series A is done and unit economics are thin. Broader QSR-storefront is too-early / chain-captive (Sweetgreen, Chipotle build their own). Watch, don't chase.
falsi: By 2027: does robotic QSR/food prep exceed ~$100M realized RaaS revenue, OR do 2+ major chains standardize on a robotic prep line (Sweetgreen/Chipotle)? Storefront-robot stall (Miso pattern) = too-early confirmed.
anti: The real production evidence is in food MANUFACTURING assembly (Chef Robotics), not flashy QSR storefronts (Miso Flippy stalled). Consensus fixates on the storefront robot; the durable wedge is back-of-house prepared-meal assembly. Mixed net — chains build captive lines (Sweetgreen), squeezing independent RaaS.
players: Chef Robotics (food-assembly RaaS — real production evidence, ~Series A), Sweetgreen Infinite Kitchen (chain-captive, deployed), Chipotle (Hyphen/autocado pilots), Nala Robotics. Miso Robotics (Flippy) — stalled, valuation cut. ARR unverified except Chef's per-meal traction.

name: Psychotherapy & Clinical Mental-Health Alliance
labor_tam: ~$50B US / $100-130B global [W] (licensed-therapist wage bill: ~600k US therapists + counselors, ~$40-50B loaded US; global $100-130B). Confirmed vs frozen. Separately a large [L] access gap — US projected short ~200k mental-health counselors by 2037; global spend ~2% of health budgets — but that latent demand is unpaid and does not convert to a displaceable wage bill.
sw_tam: Small realized ARR, est. <$50-150M category and UNVERIFIED (consumer subscription, no company discloses therapy ARR). Slingshot/Ash $93M raised, Wysa ~$35M raised — raises, not revenue. Market-research 'digital mental health' multi-$B TAMs conflate human-therapist telehealth marketplaces (BetterHelp/Talkspace), not AI. The dominant actual 'AI therapy' usage is unpriced informal general-LLM (ChatGPT/Claude) use no startup monetizes.
htc: Direct-to-consumer AI therapist: NONE — 2026 regulatory wall (4 state bans as of Jul 2026), wrongful-death liability, and zero verified ARR. Investable wedge is the WOPR-carve-out lane: clinician-augmentation / administrative support (documentation, measurement-based care, intake/triage, between-session engagement) sold B2B to provider groups and payers, seed/A ~$10-30M post. Underwrite reimbursement path + clinical evidence, not consumer subs.
falsi: By Q4 2027: BULL if a payer/health-system reimburses an autonomous AI-therapy product under a coverage/CPT code AND at least one state repeals or narrows its AI-therapy ban (the direct-to-consumer wall cracks). BEAR/base if US states banning AI therapy rise from 4 (Jul 2026) to >=8 with no reimbursement code — market stays clinician-augmentation only.
anti: Consensus chases the a16z 'AI therapist for everyone' story (Slingshot/Ash); the anti-consensus fact is that 2026 is the year the door SLAMMED — Illinois WOPR Act + NV/RI/ME outright bans, 70+ bills across 36 states, wrongful-death litigation. Therapy is the cleanest 'relational premium survives' case: the licensed human is legally protected and durable (Additive/Expansion), the DTC AI-therapist category is a regulatory/liability trap, and the largest real usage is unpriced informal ChatGPT use nobody captures.
players: Slingshot AI / Ash ($93M, a16z/Radical/Forerunner — no verified ARR); Wysa (~$35M total, clinical/employer channel); Sonia; Limbic (UK NHS triage — real deployment); Ash. Woebot wound down its consumer app 2025. Character.AI / companion bots implicated in wrongful-death suits driving the 2026 regulatory clampdown. General LLM labs (OpenAI/Anthropic) are the dominant informal substitute.

name: Real-Estate Brokerage & Property Management
labor_tam: ~$100-200B commission/fee [$] proxy (confirmed). US residential agent-commission pool ~$100-115B (NAR ~1.2-1.45M members, avg commission ~5.7% on ~$1.8-2T sales volume) + property-management fee pool. Note this is a market-revenue proxy, not a clean wage bill.
sw_tam: Proptech AI, anchored by EliseAI ($2.2B val on $250M Series E, in talks at $3.7B; platform across ~10% of US apartments — implies material, though unverified, ARR likely $100M+). Brokerage-side lead-gen/CRM/transaction copilots are a fragmented, largely incumbent-portal-adjacent layer. 97% of brokerage leaders report active agent AI use (Jan 2026) — adoption, not displacement.
htc: The residential AGENT is durable/fiduciary — commission copilots are crowded and incumbent-portal-adjacent (avoid). The real coupled-displacement wedge is PROPERTY-MANAGEMENT ops (leasing, resident comms, maintenance), but the anchor (EliseAI) is late/expensive. Seed/A ~$15-40M in vertical PM-ops for underserved asset classes (SFR, commercial, HOA) or transaction-coordination automation where a vertical isn't yet owned.
falsi: By Q4 2027: BULL if an EliseAI-class PM-ops AI is shown (audited, not vendor claim) to have cut >=20% of leasing/PM-admin headcount at a top-10 apartment operator — PM leasing is real coupled compression. BEAR if the residential commission pool stays flat-to-up (post-settlement ~5.7%) and agent headcount is stable — brokerage remains additive augmentation.
anti: Consensus frames 'the AI real-estate agent' as the disruption; the anti-consensus read is that the residential agent is one of the most durable relational/fiduciary roles (commissions went UP after the NAR settlement, not down), while the actual, quieter displacement is in property-management back-office — leasing and resident comms (EliseAI) — a different, less-glamorous pool. Brokerage = expansion/augment; PM ops = the real coupled compression, and the only place to hunt.
players: EliseAI (property-mgmt leasing/resident comms — the genuine displacement anchor, $2.2B→$3.7B val, ~10% of US apartment market); brokerage side: Compass (AI tools + Redfin coming-soon deal), Zillow (Preview launched Mar 2026, portal-data moat), Redfin; lead-intake/transaction copilots (Perspective AI, Bounti). NAR settlement is reshaping the commission structure (commissions rose, not fell).

name: Agent Ops & Fleet Supervision
labor_tam: ~$10-20B [W] net-new (frozen retained; LOW confidence — flag: this is an implied/emerging pool, the distinct 'agent supervisor' title barely exists in 2026 and is mostly folded into existing ops/platform/MLOps roles). MarketsandMarkets AI-agents $52.6B-by-2030 and similar are SOFTWARE TAMs, not the labor line — do not import.
sw_tam: AgentOps / agent-governance / observability control-plane, [$] parallel ledger (NEVER summed into the labor line). Incumbent-captured: Microsoft Agent 365 (~$15/user/mo), ServiceNow AI Control Tower, Salesforce, UiPath AgentOps; independent observability tail (AgentOps.ai, Braintrust-adjacent). Pure-play standalone ARR undisclosed/small.
htc: Mostly NONE for the labor line (diffuse headcount, not a company) and the tooling beneath it is incumbent-captured (Agent 365 + Control Tower colonizing) — a hostile standalone SW-TAM. Narrow seed wedge: managed agent-supervision-as-a-service / BPO-delivered human-in-the-loop, or vertical observability/governance where the incumbent control-plane doesn't reach (regulated, on-prem, multi-vendor fleets).
falsi: By Q4 2027: BULL if 'Agent Operations Manager'/'agent supervisor' emerges as a distinct high-volume title (e.g. >=25k US postings) with its own comp band — a real net-new occupation. BEAR if the function stays absorbed into existing MLOps/ops roles, no distinct title emerges, and the control-plane is fully owned by Microsoft/ServiceNow — W8.1 is a feature, not a labor market.
anti: Consensus (and the AgentOps vendors) forecast a large new 'humans supervising agent fleets' workforce. Anti-consensus: the pool is real but small and structurally captured — the supervision tooling is being absorbed by the same incumbents that ship the agents (Agent 365, ServiceNow Control Tower), so it is neither a big labor pool nor an independent software opportunity. And as agent reliability rises, the agents-per-supervisor ratio rises, capping headcount — it self-shrinks as the tech improves.
players: Tooling (the [$] shadow): Microsoft Agent 365, ServiceNow AI Control Tower, Salesforce Agentforce ops, UiPath, AgentOps.ai. The HUMAN line is diffuse net-new headcount inside enterprises and BPOs (fleet-ops operators, agent supervisors) — no pure-play labor vendor; the role is nascent and not yet a distinct occupation.

name: Forward-Deployed Integration / FDE
labor_tam: ~$10-18B [W] net-new (refined up from frozen $8-15B on the 2026 surge; direction is HIGH-conviction, dollar sizing is the softer part — flag: headcount is the binding uncertainty, comp anchors are solid). Comp well-anchored: Palantir FDSE median ~$211K (Levels.fyi), OpenAI/Anthropic $350-550K, 2026 median mid-level FDE ~$385K, staff ~$610K, principal ~$1.2M.
sw_tam: n/a as a track denominator — this is a pure labor line, not a software category. The relevant [$] adjacency is the internal-tools / agent-scaffolding / deployment tooling that leverages FDEs (small, fragmented).
htc: The labor line isn't a direct equity buy. Investable proxies: (1) FDE-heavy AI-native implementation boutiques (Palantir-model applied to agents) — but services margins fit VC poorly; (2) FDE-PRODUCTIVITY tooling / agent-scaffolding / deployment platforms that give leverage over the labor. Seed/A. Discipline flag: underwrite the productized/tooling leverage layer, not the raw services headcount (services-margin trap). Raw labor pool = not directly investable.
falsi: By Q4 2027: BULL if 'Forward Deployed Engineer' sustains >=50k active postings AND OpenAI Deployment Company / equivalents scale past ~1,000 FDEs with disclosed revenue — durable net-new market. BEAR if, as agents self-deploy and reliability rises, FDE demand plateaus and re-absorbs into standard solutions-engineering — a transitional bridge, not a durable occupation. Resolver: does FDE headcount keep RISING as model reliability improves (chasm durable) or fall (chasm closes)?
anti: Consensus dismisses FDE as Palantir-nostalgia or a temporary bridge that shrinks as agents improve. Anti-consensus: it is the single clearest, best-corroborated net-new labor line in the map (OpenAI built a $4B subsidiary around it) precisely BECAUSE the pilot-to-production chasm is structural, not transitional — harder-pushed capability widens the deployment gap, so FDE demand is near-term counter-cyclical to model progress. Caveat: it's labor, not software — real value, hard to capture in a venture-scalable wrapper.
players: OpenAI (launched the $4B 'OpenAI Deployment Company' subsidiary May 11 2026, built entirely around FDEs; acquired a ~150-FDE consulting firm to seed it), Anthropic, Google, Salesforce, Databricks, Palantir (originator), McKinsey QuantumBlack — all hiring FDE or equivalents. Reported ~800% YoY posting surge (report-mill figure, flagged; comp/hiring corroboration is solid).

name: Agent Evaluation, Red-Team & Safety Testing
labor_tam: $4–9B [W] net-new (refined up from frozen $3–8B on EU-enforcement live + comp inflation; Medium confidence — comp anchors solid, headcount the binding uncertainty)
sw_tam: ~$150–300M realized ARR today across pure-play eval/red-team/safety tooling ([$] parallel ledger — NEVER summed into the [W] labor line)
capture: n/a — additive/net-new, no displaced pool to capture. Penetration proxies instead: <15% of agent-deploying enterprises run a formal eval/red-team function today; independent third-party eval is concentrated at frontier labs + systemic-risk GPAI providers (evidenced by only ~a handful of vendors cited across 11 system cards). Tooling-category realized ARR (~$150–300M) is a fraction of the multi-$B implied labor line — i.e., most eval work is still done by in-house humans, not bought as software.
htc: Seed/A, ~$15–40M post — but AVOID the crowded frontier-lab-facing generic red-team tooling: Gray Swan (A), Patronus (B, ~$475M), Irregular (A, Sequoia), Braintrust (B, ~$800M) are seed-closed and M&A-exit-destined (Robust Intelligence→Cisco template). The open door is the ADJACENT white-space where the regulatory-independence mandate bites and generic tools don't fit: (1) regulated-vertical eval (healthcare/finance/legal agent testing); (2) continuous POST-deployment production eval/monitoring (as Art. 55 forces ongoing, not just pre-release, testing); (3) the expert red-teamer SUPPLY marketplace feeding Arena-style crowdsourcing. Underwrite the structural conflict-of-interest moat (a GPAI provider cannot self-certify its own safety) that neither model labs nor security incumbents can fill by definition.
falsi: By 2027-08-02 (EU AI Act Art. 55 full-compliance deadline for pre-existing GPAI): (a) ≥1 public EU enforcement action or fine for inadequate adversarial testing AND (b) major frontier releases still cite ≥2 INDEPENDENT third-party red-team vendors (Gray Swan/Irregular-class) per system card → BULL: the regulatory demand floor AND the independence moat both hold, third-party eval labor is a durable net-new market (raise conviction to High). If neither holds by that date — EU enforcement deferred/toothless (GPAI code-of-practice softening) and labs internalize eval so third-party citations drop → BEAR: L→5 (lab-captured), the category collapses into incumbents/OSS, standalone eval loses its protected niche.
anti: Consensus holds two opposing-but-both-wrong views: bulls fund eval as a hot startup category (aggregators claim it took ~35% of AI-safety capital), bears treat safety as a cost center that self-solves as models get safer. Both miss the durable truth — this track is the ANTI-C1 HEDGE: verification/eval demand is structurally COUNTER-CYCLICAL to the agent thesis. The wider the revenue-vs-delivered-value gap stays (METR −4% CI[−15,+9]; realized capture 0.1–11%), the MORE eval labor is needed — so W8.3 pays off precisely when the rest of the map disappoints. Second contrarian point: capital is misallocated — it floods the TOOLING layer (which OSS-deflates via PyRIT/Garak and gets incumbent-acquired), while the durable value is the net-new LABOR plus the regulatory-independence requirement that CANNOT be automated away or self-certified. The non-obvious moat is a structural conflict-of-interest (you can't grade your own safety), not a data/tech moat — which is why labs pay third parties despite building eval in-house.

name: AI Training-Data & Labeling / Expert Sourcing
sw_tam: $2–6.5B [$] (net platform take ~$2–2.5B; gross marketplace GMV ~$6.3B)
capture: Bifurcated, no single clean rate. Commodity tier: ~80% of labeling VOLUME now machine pre-labeled (high task-automation, but on a low-wage pool so small dollar displacement) — MTurk retired, 33–46% of crowd workers already using LLMs. Expert/frontier tier: net-new CREATION, not capture — top-7 platforms pay ≈$4M+/day to human contributors (Mercor alone ~$2M/day to 30k weekly-active experts).
htc: Horizontal expert-sourcing marketplaces are CLOSED to a seed/A check — all late-stage (Surge $15–25B, Mercor $20B talks, Scale $29B, Handshake $1B+ gross). Per frozen P3 pick #5, hunt the adjacent white-space instead: (1) VERTICAL/domain expert-data specialists — robotics-teleoperation & embodied-action data (directly maps to the HTC robotics thesis and the CyberOrigin data-layer anchor — the physical-world expert-data wedge is the least-crowded and most-defensible), plus medical, legal, and defense frontier-data; (2) RL-ENVIRONMENT + proprietary-EVAL-set tooling (the "graduate from undifferentiated supply / no switching cost" moat that Handshake is buying Cleanlab to get, and the anti-C1 verification hedge). Target seed/A at ~$10–60M post. The commodity-annotation layer is uninvestable (deflating). Verdict on horizontals: none — proven / late-stage, seed door closed.
falsi: By Q4-2027: do the 3 independent expert-data platforms (Mercor + Surge + Handshake) hold combined GROSS-revenue growth >50% YoY AND each keep ≥2 of the top-4 frontier labs as NEUTRAL customers (no Meta/Scale-style vertical takeover)? YES → durable net-new expert-labor market; raise conviction, treat W8.4 as a real W8 labor-creation track. If independent-platform growth stalls <20% YoY, OR ≥2 top labs internalize expert-sourcing in-house / pivot spend to synthetic + RL-environments, OR Scale's 2027 revenue keeps falling below $1B → the frontier-data boom was a transient RLHF super-cycle; W8.4 recompresses toward the deflating commodity tier (bear).
anti: Two contrarian reads. (1) The headline "Mercor/Surge $1–2B ARR" is a MARKETPLACE GROSS flow — 60–70% is pass-through to contractors; Mercor's real net take is ~$360–500M, so the "$2B ARR" overstates the company ~4–5x. This is a take-rate labor business, not a software-margin one — never bank it as SaaS ARR (this is the freeze's Mercor flag, now sharpened: verified-as-gross, not verified-as-ARR). (2) Deeper: the frontier-data super-cycle is self-terminating scaffolding. It exists to close the exact model value-gaps that, once closed, reduce the need for it — and RL-environments + synthetic data already auto-handle ~80% of volume. The bull thesis ("largest net-new AI labor market") and the bear thesis ("transient RLHF crutch the models will obsolete") are the SAME fact viewed twice. Also: Scale — the incumbent that "won" — was kneecapped not by a rival but by its own lab investor (Meta), because any lab-owned vendor loses every other lab; NEUTRALITY is the moat and it structurally caps consolidation.

name: Agent Trust, Insurance & Audit
labor_tam: ~$2-5B [W] net-new (frozen retained; LOW confidence — embryonic. Only ~5 dedicated AI-liability insurance products exist worldwide as of early 2026; premiums tiny). The audit/assurance headcount could grow materially on EU AI Act conformity demand, but is not yet a sizable payroll line.
sw_tam: Straddles insurance capital + AI-risk-assessment IP. Standalone AI-liability products: Armilla (Lloyd's coverholder, up to $25M/org, 500+ AI evaluations), Munich Re aiSure (via Mosaic, up to $15M), Testudo (Lloyd's Lab, up to $9.25M). Feb 2026 Armilla+Chaucer 'Vanguard AI' bundles AI liability with cyber/tech-E&O — the tell that AI risk is being absorbed into existing lines, not spun standalone.
htc: The investable wedge is the MGA/coverholder + AI-certification model (Armilla): a startup owns AI-risk-underwriting IP and a proprietary loss/eval data flywheel while incumbent Lloyd's/reinsurer capital carries balance-sheet risk. Seed/A ~$10-30M. Adjacent: AI-audit/assurance-as-a-service tied to EU AI Act conformity. Flag: very early (Low conviction), premiums tiny; the audit-labor line itself isn't directly investable — underwrite the data moat, not the premium.
falsi: By 2027 (as insurers accumulate loss data + EU AI Act GPAI enforcement bites): BULL if standalone AI-liability premium written globally crosses ~$500M AND a startup MGA (Armilla-class) builds a durable loss-ratio-backed book — a real net-new market with a startup wedge. BEAR if AI risk keeps getting absorbed into cyber/tech-E&O (the 'Vanguard AI' bundling pattern generalizes) and dedicated AI insurers stay sub-scale — a rider on existing lines, not a category.
anti: Consensus is bimodal — AI-insurance boosters ('a new multi-billion category') vs skeptics ('insurers will just exclude AI'). Anti-consensus: the tell is Chaucer's 'Vanguard AI' bundle — AI risk is being absorbed into cyber/E&O, not spun into a standalone line, capping the pure-play. The durable startup wedge is NOT the insurance capital (incumbent Lloyd's/Munich Re) but the AI-risk-assessment/certification data moat (Armilla's 500+ evals become actuarial gold). It's also a leading indicator — dedicated AI insurance only scales once real agent-failure losses hit balance sheets; today it prices tail risk blind.
players: Armilla AI (Lloyd's/Chaucer-backed, MGA + AI certification, 500+ evals — the startup wedge); Munich Re aiSure (incumbent, since 2018); Testudo (Lloyd's Lab); Chaucer/Lloyd's (risk capital). Some insurers cover hallucinations, others explicitly exclude AI — the market is splitting in 2026.

name: Context & AI-Engineering Labor (job creation)
labor_tam: $4–9B [W] net-new (additive) — modest upward nudge from frozen $3–8B on 2026 comp inflation (US AI-SWE avg $245k) and LinkedIn-#1 / Upwork +109% momentum
sw_tam: ~$0.3–0.8B 2026 category ARR (context/eval/agent-engineering tooling) — fragmented, sub-scale, fast-growing; logged as a [$] leading-indicator proxy, NEVER summed into the labor map
capture: n/a — additive creation track, no coupled capture-rate. The tooling [$] captures <1% of the created wage bill (~$0.3–0.8B SW ARR vs ~$4–9B labor). The value story is inverted vs displacement tracks: value accrues to the net-new WORKERS, not to a displacing vendor.
htc: Mostly seed-closed at the leaders. The labor itself isn't investable; the proxy tooling leaders are past seed (LangChain $1.25B Series B; eval/observability leaders Series B+). Thin seed/A white-space remains ADJACENT: proprietary agent-eval-set marketplaces, agent-memory/context infra, and vertical context-engineering-as-a-service — enter ~$15–60M post ONLY on a defensible eval-data or expert-supply moat, NOT horizontal LangChain-clones (OSS + lab-native tooling compress them). Cleanest HTC expression runs through W8.3 eval / W8.4 expert-sourcing (the anti-C1 hedge), not W8.6 pure context labor.
falsi: By Jan-2028 (LinkedIn "Jobs on the Rise 2028" + Levels.fyi AI-SWE postings/comp): BULL if "AI / agent / context engineer" stays a top-5 fastest-growing US role AND net-new agent-engineering wage bill clears ~$10B (headcount×comp). BEAR if "context engineer" falls off the Jobs-on-the-Rise list and AI-SWE postings flatten YoY — the "prompt engineer" 2024 fade repeating — meaning the offset is transitional and absorbs into general SWE (W1.1a), capping ~$5–8B. Interim check: LinkedIn Jobs-on-the-Rise Jan-2027 ranking of AI Engineer.
anti: Consensus = "AI destroys jobs." The shallow anti-consensus is "W8.6 proves AI also CREATES a well-paid new profession (AI Engineer #1 fastest-growing, $245k)." The sharper anti-consensus: this is the one labor market whose buyer is also its own substitute — agents increasingly self-manage context/memory/RAG, so "context engineer" is likely the "prompt engineer" of 2026 (a title that peaked '23 and dissolved into general SWE by '25). Creation here is real but structurally self-cannibalizing and probably near-peak. The DURABLE creation is EVAL / expert-data (W8.3/W8.4 — model-independent verification, the genuine anti-C1 hedge), NOT pure context-engineering labor. Bet the hedge on eval, not on context engineers.

name: Rideshare, Taxi & Robotaxi
labor_tam: $0.3-0.5T [W] confirmed (US-weighted for-hire driver wage bill; low comp-per-head, dollar-weighting de-emphasizes vs headcount).
sw_tam: ~$0.5-1.5B global robotaxi ride/service revenue 2026 ([$] proxy, not labor capture): Waymo ~$355M annualized (Feb-26) tracking toward ~$1B at 1M weekly rides; Baidu Apollo Go 100M+ cumulative rides; Pony robotaxi rev only $12.1M in Q2-26 (+691% off tiny base).
htc: None at the vehicle layer — capex-in-the-billions, big-tech/OEM captured (Alphabet, Tesla, Amazon, Baidu). Adjacent seed surface = AV remote-operations/teleop, safety-case/simulation data, and fleet-ops software feeding the crowned stacks.
falsi: Does Waymo hit its stated 1M weekly paid rides (~$1B annualized) by Q4-2026? Q4-26 median forecasts sit ~713K, short of target; a miss confirms the multi-year capex-grind read. Also watch any US metro posting measurable net taxi/rideshare-driver headcount decline in BLS/city data by mid-2027.
anti: Tesla-bull consensus treats 'widespread driverless 2026' as imminent mass displacement. Even the leader (Waymo) is ~$355M annualized on <0.5% capture, net driver headcount is still RISING (gig growth), and this is a decade capex grind not a 2026 event. Apply the Unitree rule: never convert robotaxi valuations or ride-count headlines into deployed labor displacement.
players: Waymo (Alphabet, ~500-713K weekly rides 2026, 5+ new metros); Tesla robotaxi (~700K paid miles since Jun-25, still partly supervised, 7-city H1-26 push — discount Musk 'widespread by EOY26'); Baidu Apollo Go; Pony.ai (fleet target 3,500, ~1,975 live); WeRide; Zoox (Amazon). Realized capture <1% of driver pool.

name: Long-haul & Regional Trucking
labor_tam: $0.5-0.9T [W] confirmed (US heavy-truck driver wage bill; wages/benefits ~43c of every operating dollar at large TL carriers). Note: only ~40% line-haul slice is AV-addressable near-term.
sw_tam: <$100M commercial autonomous-trucking revenue 2026 (pre-scale): Kodiak ~$30M+ recognized but mostly US-military + oilfield, not mass line-haul; Aurora early per-mile/driverless. Per-mile/driver-as-a-service model still forming.
htc: None at AV-developer layer — leaders are public/late-stage (Aurora, Kodiak) and capital-intensive; not model-lab, not seed-ownable. Adjacent seed = freight-dispatch voice agents (HappyRobot cross-ref W3.6), autonomous-lane insurance, teleop/remote-supervision.
falsi: Does any operator reach true driver-out (no safety observer) commercial scale >500 trucks by end-2026 (Aurora target 200+; Kodiak driver-out goal EOY26)? If the ATA driver shortage stays >80K through 2026 (currently ~82K, →175K by 2028), displacement thesis stays gap-filling, not net-cut.
anti: Consensus flips between 'trucking is the first mass AV displacement' and '5-10% of lanes by 2032.' HTC read: near-term this is SHORTAGE-FILLING not displacement (chronic ~82K deficit → low backlash, like SOC), and only the ~40% line-haul slice is addressable — so the coupled-capturable dollars are far below the $0.5-0.9T family pool. Real production evidence is thin (hundreds of trucks), so discount aggressive displacement per the MIT-production-evidence rule.
players: Aurora (public; 100K+ driverless mi, 2 lanes incl. 600mi FTW-El Paso, target 200+ trucks & observerless kit EOY26; Hirschbach/Werner/Schneider/FedEx/Uber Freight); Kodiak AI (public via SPAC/S-1; 15,600+ revenue loads by Q1-26, driver-out goal EOY26); Waabi (Volvo VNL platform transfer, pre-commercial). Deployment = hundreds of trucks vs ~2M drivers → capture ~0%.

name: Last-mile Delivery & Courier
labor_tam: $0.3-0.6T [W] confirmed (last-mile courier/gig-delivery wage bill; low comp-per-head).
sw_tam: ~$100-250M global delivery-robot service revenue 2026 (largely pilot-subsidized): fee-per-delivery model, sub-scale unit economics. Report-mill '$50B last-mile robotics market' is TAM-not-revenue.
htc: Thin — lead players past seed & capital-heavy (Nuro $6B, Serve public, Coco $80M+). Adjacent seed = delivery-fleet teleop/remote-ops software, RaaS orchestration for regional operators, drone airspace/ops — the software layer, not the hardware OEM.
falsi: Does Coco hit its 10,000-robot target by end-2026 (from low-single-digit thousands)? Does any operator publish delivery unit-economics beating human-courier cost? Sustained pilot-subsidy through 2026 = displacement deferred.
anti: The '$50B last-mile robotics market' headline conflates TAM with deployed labor capture. Reality: net courier headcount is still RISING on the q-commerce boom, robots are pilot-subsidized at <0.5% capture, and drones remain FAA-gated. Real but slow physical grind; sidewalk-robot state-law liberalization (30+ states) is the leading indicator to track, not the market-size reports.
players: Coco Robotics ($80M raise 2025, Altman bros; 500K+ deliveries; 10,000-robot EOY26 target — unverified); Serve Robotics (public; 1,000 3rd-gen robots, Uber Eats/7-Eleven); Nuro ($203M @ $6B val, pivoted to 'Nuro Driver' licensing); Starship ($339M); Zipline ($1.75B, drones); Amazon/Rivian. Capture <0.5%.

name: Structured-Cell Manipulation & Production
labor_tam: ~$4.2T [W] structured-environment manipulation (machine-tending W5.3, piece-pick/pack W5.2, structured food/bev W5.7, offsite prefab W5.6) + net-new lab/pharma & precision micro-assembly (~$20–40B). NON-ADDITIVE re-cut of W5 — counted once, never summed with W5.
sw_tam: Industrial-automation incumbent + integrator stack (FANUC/ABB/KUKA/Siemens); ~$30–40B captured today ≈ the map's physical capture ceiling.
capture: ~1–1.5% (map ceiling; ~0.9M machine-tending robots ≈ 20% of 4.66M industrial stock, ~$30–40B / ~$2.0–2.8T pool). Everywhere else in Family P capture rounds to zero.
htc: OEM/integrator layer is incumbent-owned + capital-heavy — NOT the seed wedge. Investable adjacency is the data/commissioning layer (P8), not the arm.
falsi: Machine-tending-robot installed base > ~1.3M units by 2028 with disclosed labor-avoidance = accelerating capture.
anti: The one physical cell where displacement is actually real — but value accrues to industrial-automation incumbents/integrators, not startups; a smarter cross-embodiment 'brain' commoditizes the model and hands margin to the OEM.

name: Bounded-Space Mobility & Frontline Service-Physical
labor_tam: ~$1.05T [W] mobility + light-manip in mapped bounded spaces (warehouse AMR W5.1, commercial floor cleaning W5.5) + physical slice of retail/food-service (W10 overlay-stamped, not summed). NON-ADDITIVE re-cut.
sw_tam: AMR OEMs; Amazon internalized 1M+ robots (surfaces as avoided hiring, not vendor ARR).
capture: <1%; structurally understated (Amazon internalized robotics = avoided hiring, not ARR).
htc: Seed door largely closed in horizontal AMR; live wedges are vertical/edge-case mobility + the fleet-ops software layer (→P8).
falsi: Sidewalk/indoor delivery-robot fleets clear unit-economics at >~10k sustained commercial units by 2028.
anti: 'Warehouse robots are a land grab' — but the horizontal AMR door is already closed (Amazon 1M+ internalized); remaining seed room is vertical edge-cases and fleet software, not another AMR OEM.

name: Open-Road Autonomous Mobility (AV / Transport)
labor_tam: ~$1.55T [W] driver wage bill on public roads (robotaxi W9.1, trucking W9.2, last-mile W9.3). NON-ADDITIVE re-cut of W9. AV hardware/compute/RaaS is [$] capital, never summed.
sw_tam: AV stack + RaaS [$] capex (Waymo/Aurora/Kodiak); AV remote-assist teleop ~$0.55B 2026 (report-mill, direction only).
capture: <1%; decade-long tail (only ~40% line-haul AV-addressable near-term). Gate is R=5 safety-case/liability, not dexterity.
htc: Capex/RaaS, not a labor-software seed market; value in the AV stack ([$]) and teleop-assist (→P8).
falsi: Driverless trucking revenue-miles cross a disclosed commercial threshold on interstate lanes by 2028.
anti: The gate is regulatory/liability, not the driving model — which is why P3 is split from P2 despite both being 'locomotion'; a better model doesn't move the safety-case clock.

name: Unstructured Dexterous & Field Manipulation
labor_tam: ~$5.3T [W] gross-to-fine manipulation in open/novel environments, non-human-contact (skilled trades W6.1, unstructured construction W6.2, field service W6.4, unstructured janitorial W6.5). NON-ADDITIVE re-cut of W6. LARGEST notional pool with ~0 realized capture.
sw_tam: n/a — hardware-timeline-blocked; better VLAs help perception, but the dexterity/hardware gate dominates.
capture: ~0% (too-early). The clearest 'huge pool, hardware-timeline-blocked' cell — do NOT read the $5.3T as addressable.
htc: Not a seed-software question — a robotics-timeline question (5–15 yr). Watch π-class dexterity milestones, not app-layer startups.
falsi: A general-purpose site/field manipulator clears a real trade task at >~80% autonomous success outside a demo by 2028.
anti: The $5.3T headline is the biggest trap on the map: near-zero capturable for 5–15 years regardless of model IQ — the gate is actuation/dexterity/cost/MTBF, not the brain.

name: Deformable & Contact-Rich Manipulation
labor_tam: ~$1.3T [W] thin/slippery/deformable + contact-rich manipulation (specialty-crop harvest W6.6, food prep/QSR W6.7, textile/garment sewing, laundry, hotel housekeeping soft-goods W10 overlay, protein/food-processing). NON-ADDITIVE re-cut.
sw_tam: n/a — the dexterity frontier; no mass-market laundry/food robot.
capture: ~0%. NARROW-CROSSED / GENERAL-BLOCKED: π0 >80% on known-garment T-shirt folding (narrow), general deformable (arbitrary fabric/food) undemonstrated. The one place physical dexterity is measurably moving.
htc: The falsifiable indicator IS the cell: does deformable generalization move from known-garment folding to ARBITRARY fabric/food at >80% by ~2028?
falsi: Arbitrary (not known-garment) deformable manipulation clears >80% success by ~2028 → P5 begins to convert; else stays a research frontier.
anti: Isolated as its own watch-cell precisely because it's the single measurable dexterity mover (π0 folding) — but 'narrow crossed' is not 'general solved'; there is still no laundry robot.

name: Human-Contact Care & Physical Assistance
labor_tam: ~$1.1T [W] paid + ~$11T informal [L] — fine manipulation with direct sustained human physical contact (personal care/ADL, patient handling, rehab; W6.3). NON-ADDITIVE re-cut. NOTE: the ~$11T [L] is the SAME pool as W14.1 — never sum the two latent tails.
sw_tam: n/a — highest safety/trust/licensing gate; augmentation (lift-assist, monitoring) on durable human labor.
capture: ~0%. Distinctive tailwind: INVERTED social license under demographic-shortage mandates (Japan ~11M gap, Korea) → near-zero displacement politics → least-friction embodied-AI deployment path despite the hardest capability gate.
htc: The cell that directly feeds the HTC robotics thesis — but the investable expression is the data/teleop layer under the shortage mandate (P8), not the care-robot OEM.
falsi: A care robot performs an unsupervised ADL task (transfer/toileting/feeding) at clinical-safety threshold in a real facility by 2028.
anti: Care is the hardest capability gate yet the LEAST-friction deployment path — because inverted social license (shortage mandates) removes the displacement backlash that blocks everywhere else.

name: Embodied Sensing, Inspection & Security
labor_tam: ~$0.5T [W] + large [L] — perception-dominant low-manip autonomy: commercial security/guarding, autonomous rounds, infra/energy/mining inspection, structured visual QC (W5.4), defense ISR/logistics (W12.2, sovereign R5). Largely NET-NEW [W]+[L] folded here; W5.4/W12.2 re-homed once.
sw_tam: Site/telemetry data + integration moat (physical twin of the SOC data moat). Knightscope ~$7–11/hr vs $25–45/hr human guard.
capture: <1%. Structural shape = W1.8 SOC: compression of the staffed guard/inspector rung + [L] expansion into never-patrolled coverage.
htc: The structural MIRROR of the SOC hunting ground in the physical world — most-deployed-today band (actuation is light). Wedge = detection/site-telemetry data + fleet-supervision layer (understaffed → no displacement backlash), NOT the patrol-robot chassis.
falsi: A pure-play security-robot fleet discloses >~$100M retained ARR at coverage-hours a guard force can't match by Q4-2027.
anti: Everyone watches humanoids; the deployed embodied money is in boring perception-dominant security/inspection — because sensing is far easier than acting, and the moat is site-telemetry data, not the chassis.

name: Robot-Economy Labor (teleop / supervision / data-verify / sim)
labor_tam: ~$5–15B [W] net-new, >100% YoY — the human wage bill the robot economy CREATES (physical twin of W8): teleop-as-a-service + embodied-data collection, robot fleet remote supervision ('wrangler'), robot commissioning/field-maintenance (physical FDE), embodied-data frame-verification, sim/scenario authoring. NET-NEW — outside the $15T displaceable base.
sw_tam: Managed-service teleop forming (AV teleop ~$0.55B 2026, robot-teleop-cloud $4.2B 2025 — [$] service proxies, not the labor line). Robot hardware/compute [$], out; only headcount lands in P8.
capture: n/a (no displaced pool — additive creation, like W8, never subtracted or summed into the $15T).
htc: THE thesis layer: the one part of the physical stack that is (a) capability-gating for everyone, (b) hardware-decoupled, (c) labor/process-scaled not capex-scaled, (d) not yet incumbent-captured. CyberOrigin (HTC portfolio anchor) sits here — frame-verified embodied data. The map missed it because it tracked physical displacement but had no physical CREATION family.
falsi: Does frame-verified embodied-data revenue (CyberOrigin/AgiBot/1X-class) sustain >100% YoY into 2027 — or does synthetic/sim data collapse the human-teleop wage bill before it scales?
anti: The investable layer isn't the humanoid OEM (bubble: Unitree ~$9B not $50B, no fleet >low-hundreds) — it's the hardware-decoupled data/teleop/verification layer underneath, which every OEM and lab needs and none has captured.

name: In-person Consumer & Personal Services (thin cell)
labor_tam: ~$3–6T [W] formal paid in-person personal services (hairdressing/beauty, fitness/personal training, paid childcare & early-ed aides, pet care, funeral, personal/event service staff). The map's largest named-track under-fill (W3 prior $8–12T vs named ~$2.3T). Opened for MECE completeness + to de-bias the dollar-weighted headline. Additive — was previously uncounted.
sw_tam: ~none — no vendor pins a production wage-replacing metric; booking/scheduling SaaS only.
capture: ≈0% (trust + physical-presence gate). Not investable; a headcount-companion carve-in.
htc: NOT a seed hunting ground — trust/presence gate makes capture≈0. Tracked for completeness and to de-bias the total-TAM headline.
falsi: A funded vendor pins a production wage-replacing (not scheduling/booking) metric in personal services by Q4-2027 → re-underwrite; base case no → stays a headcount-companion carve-in.
anti: The map's biggest hole isn't a hot new AI market — it's a $3–6T in-person services tail the dollar-weighted lens hid and AI can't touch (presence+trust gate). Naming it de-biases 'total agent TAM'; it is completeness, not opportunity.
